verdict.rationale: LangGraph's interrupt() mechanism explicitly pauses graph execution at a node to wait for external input, and execution is resumed by re-invoking the graph with a Command carrying the human's decision, which becomes the interrupt() return value — directly matching the story. This is reinforced by checkpointer-based persistence for human-in-the-loop workflows and GitHub's dedicated 'Human-in-the-loop' feature callout, plus community corroboration describing LangGraph's state-machine support for human-in-the-loop with time travel. Missing for 10: independent hands-on validation of the interrupt/resume flow itself (community comments discuss HITL generally but don't confirm this specific mechanic works flawlessly in production).
